text:
Tyler Seguin hasn't scored in eleven games, and our numbers say he's earned better. He has 3 goals on 5.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 6% when our range for his true rate runs from about 10% to 15%. The Stars have scored 6.4 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. Over the drought he's had 2.7 expected goals, which is enough looks that the cold spell reads as bad luck rather than decline.

The encouraging part is the volume. At 34, after only 27 games last season, he's generating 1.09 expected goals per 60, up from 0.61, on 14:53 a night in a middle-six role. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (a small, six-game sample) had him on the end of passes across the slot and setting up plenty of shots himself.

He came into the season with 367 career goals and a 2011 Stanley Cup from his Boston days, and Dallas has kept winning without his scoring. Our projection still gives him 11 to 21 goals. The day the shots start falling, the totals will move quickly.
